Question B-006-005-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Standing waves are evidence of reflected energy on the line. Reflected energy is not delivered to the antenna on the first pass, so the transfer of RF energy to the antenna is reduced.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "perfect impedance match between transmitter and transmission line": A transmitter-to-line match only says the transmitter is matched to the line impedance. Standing waves on the line are caused by a mismatch between the line and the antenna or load, so this choice does not explain standing waves being present.
- sourceIndex 2: "maximum transfer of energy to the antenna from the transmitter": Maximum transfer occurs when the antenna system is matched and reflections are minimized; standing waves indicate that some energy is being reflected.
- sourceIndex 3: "lack of radiation from the transmission line": Standing waves describe voltage and current variations along the line; they do not mean the transmission line cannot radiate or that radiation from it is absent.
